issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to a function named create_zero_state(...) for initializing an MPS zero state, but the template repository provides a function named init_zero_state(...) instead. This name mismatch is structural — students following the problem statement will try to implement or call create_zero_state, but the template offers a differently named entry point, which will cause confusion and impediments when integrating student code with the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across artifacts. Rename the template's init_zero_state(...) to create_zero_state(...), or alternatively update the problem statement and solution to reference init_zero_state(...). Ensure the function signature and return type remain the same (list of rank-3 tensors) so students and automated tests use the same API.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a function named create_zero_state for the tensor-network part, but the template repository defines the equivalent stub as init_zero_state. This mismatch makes it unclear for students where to implement the required create_zero_state behavior and can cause confusion when tests or instructions refer to create_zero_state while the template provides init_zero_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function init_zero_state to create_zero_state to match the problem statement and solution, or add a small wrapper in the template: def create_zero_state(num_qubits): return init_zero_state(num_qubits). This keeps the required identifier consistent with instructions and tests.
